title: Geometric inverse image and constant left-module scalar extension
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be small sites, with sheaf values and all indexing categories in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Let $f:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ be a geometric morphism, that is, an adjunction $L=f^{-1}\dashv f_*$ whose left adjoint preserves finite limits. Let $a:R\to S$ be a unital homomorphism of rings, not necessarily commutative. Use constant ring sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] and the canonical constant left-module lifts $L_R,L_S$ of [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image]. Write $E_a^{\mathcal C},E_a^{\mathcal D}$ for sheafification of sectionwise left scalar extension, as in [def-pod-ring-scalar-extension]. Then there is a natural isomorphism of left $S$-module sheaves
$$L_SE_a^{\mathcal C}M\xrightarrow{\sim}E_a^{\mathcal D}L_RM.$$
It sends the inverse image of every sheafified pure tensor $s\otimes m$ to $s\otimes L_Rm$, where inverse images of local sections mean their adjunction-unit images and constants are identified by the canonical constant-ring maps. For every left $R$-module $Q$, there is a natural isomorphism
$$\underline{S\otimes_R Q}_{\mathcal C}\xrightarrow{\sim}E_a^{\mathcal C}\underline Q_{\mathcal C},$$
sending a constant pure tensor $s\otimes q$ to the sheafification-unit tensor of the constant sections $s,q$. These statements require neither flatness nor finiteness. Module sheaves use [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

source.place: Tag 03CZ, lemma-adjointness-tensor-restrict, with its sectionwise adjunction and sheafification proof; agent-formulated geometric inverse-image and constant-module consequences for arbitrary left coefficients.

proof.text:
Write $U_a$ for scalar restriction. For any presheaf $P$ of left $R$-modules and sheaf $N$ of left $S$-modules, the scalar-extension universal property, object by object, gives
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{S,\mathrm{PSh}}(S\otimes_R P,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{R,\mathrm{PSh}}(P,U_aN).$$
Explicitly $v$ goes to $m\mapsto v(1\otimes m)$ and $w$ goes to $s\otimes m\mapsto s w(m)$. The latter respects $s a(r)\otimes m=s\otimes rm$ since $w(rm)=a(r)w(m)$; restriction compatibility on one side is equivalent to restriction compatibility on the other by these formulas. Restricting scalars leaves a sheaf a sheaf, since it changes none of its underlying abelian groups or restriction maps. Sheafification's factorization property therefore gives
$$\operatorname{Hom}_S((S\otimes_RP)^\#,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{R,\mathrm{PSh}}(P,U_aN).$$
For a sheaf $P=M$ this is $E_a\dashv U_a$; its unit $j_M$ is $m\mapsto[1\otimes m]$. Both bijections are natural, as precomposition replaces $m$ by its image and postcomposition replaces $w(m)$ by its image. This argument applies on either site.

source.place: Tag 03CZ, lemma-adjointness-tensor-restrict, proof via the presheaf adjunction; arbitrary-left-ring variant from def-pod-ring-scalar-extension

proof.text:
Let $f_{*,R}$ and $f_{*,S}$ be the right adjoints in the normalized constant-module lifts, and $V$ forgetting scalars. The transport statement gives $Vf_{*,\Lambda}=f_*V$ with forgotten unit the abelian unit $\eta$, and $L_\Lambda$ acts on $f^{-1}VM$ by $f^{-1}(\lambda_r)$. Forgetting the triangle identity gives $f_*(V\varepsilon_N)\circ\eta_{f_*N}=\mathrm{id}$, so the forgotten module counit $V\varepsilon_N$ is the abelian counit $\varepsilon^{\mathrm{ab}}_N$. Its $\Lambda$-linearity reads $\varepsilon^{\mathrm{ab}}_N\circ f^{-1}(\lambda_r^{f_{*,\Lambda}N})=\lambda_r^N\circ\varepsilon^{\mathrm{ab}}_N$; taking abelian adjuncts, $\lambda_r^{f_{*,\Lambda}N}=f_*(\lambda_r^N)$ for every $r\in\Lambda$. Consequently
$$U_a^{\mathcal C} f_{*,S}\cong f_{*,R}U_a^{\mathcal D}$$
by the identity on underlying abelian sheaves: for every $r\in R$ the scalar endomorphism on both sides is $f_*(\lambda_{a(r)})$, and addition, zero and negation are identical. The constant-ring maps commute with $a$ because both send a constant $r$ to $a(r)$; their equality follows by the universal property of the sheafification of the constant ring presheaf. Thus the identity is linear over the constant ring sheaf, natural in $N$, and preserves the underlying adjunction-unit identifications.

source.place: Tag 00YV, proposition-functoriality-algebraic-structures-topoi, fixed-ring scalar-endomorphism construction and lifted adjunction

proof.text:
For every $S$-module sheaf $N$ on $\mathcal D$, combine step 1, the lifted module adjunctions, and step 2:
$$\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Hom}_S(L_SE_a^{\mathcal C}M,N)&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_S(E_a^{\mathcal C}M,f_{*,S}N)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,U_a^{\mathcal C}f_{*,S}N)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,f_{*,R}U_a^{\mathcal D}N)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_R(L_RM,U_a^{\mathcal D}N)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_S(E_a^{\mathcal D}L_RM,N).
\end{aligned}$$
All bijections are natural in $M,N$. The cited co-Yoneda statement supplies an isomorphism $E_a^{\mathcal D}L_RM\to L_SE_a^{\mathcal C}M$ representing this bijection. Take its inverse $c_M$ for the direction in the item. Naturality in $M$ follows by the uniqueness clause of the same statement, applied to the two composites for a morphism $M\to M'$.

source.place: Tag 001P, lemma-yoneda, applied to the opposite category and the displayed composite adjunction bijection

proof.text:
The normalized lift also gives the identity-underlying-sheaf comparison $U_a^{\mathcal D}L_S\cong L_RU_a^{\mathcal C}$: both transport the scalar $r$ as $L(\lambda_{a(r)})$. Following the five bijections of step 3 on the identity map gives the unit equation
$$U_a^{\mathcal D}(c_M)\circ L_R(j_M)=j_{L_RM}.$$
Indeed each scalar adjunction evaluates at $1\otimes-$, each geometric adjunction takes the underlying adjunct, and step 2 is the identity there; the triangle identities cancel the intervening geometric unit and counit. Thus the inverse image of $[1\otimes m]$ maps to $[1\otimes L_Rm]$. As $c_M$ is $S$-linear and the lift carries the constant scalar $s$ to the same $s$, it maps the inverse image of $[s\otimes m]=s[1\otimes m]$ to $[s\otimes L_Rm]$. This is an equality of the sheafification-unit and adjunction-unit morphisms, so it interprets local sections exactly as in the statement, without assuming a site functor or a pointwise formula for $f^{-1}$.

source.place: Tag 00YV, lifted adjunction with underlying unit; scalar adjunction units of Tag 03CZ

proof.text:
Apply the presheaf version of step 1 to the constant presheaf $P=Q$. For an $S$-module sheaf $N$ on $\mathcal C$ there are natural bijections
$$\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Hom}_S(E_a^{\mathcal C}\underline Q,N)&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_R(\underline Q,U_aN)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{R,\mathrm{PSh}}(Q_{\mathrm{const}},U_aN)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{S,\mathrm{PSh}}((S\otimes_R Q)_{\mathrm{const}},N)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_S(\underline{S\otimes_R Q},N).
\end{aligned}$$
The second and fourth bijections are precisely the sheafification universal property defining the constant sheaves; sectionwise scalar extension of a constant presheaf is the displayed constant presheaf. Co-Yoneda gives an isomorphism $\underline{S\otimes_RQ}\to E_a^{\mathcal C}\underline Q$, natural in $Q$ by uniqueness. This does not assume that the site has a terminal object.

source.place: Tag 03CZ, presheaf-to-sheaf adjunction proof; Tag 001P, co-Yoneda

proof.text: For the isomorphism of step 5, put $N=E_a^{\mathcal C}\underline Q$ and follow its identity through that chain. The result is the sheafified morphism of presheaves $s\otimes q\mapsto s\,j_{\underline Q}(q)$, where $q$ first enters the constant sheaf by its sheafification unit. This is exactly the required constant pure-tensor formula. All arguments used universal properties and the exact normalized lift, never exactness of scalar extension. In particular $S=0$, $Q=0$, the identity ring map, and nonflat quotients such as $\mathbf Z\to\mathbf Z/2$ obey the same formulas; arbitrary noncommutative rings obey the same left-balancing identity from step 1.
